note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • Persistent fever with alternating sweats/chills for 7 days after recent travel to rural Vietnam (returned 4 weeks ago).  
  • No specific food, drug, or environmental trigger identified.

- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Day 0 (7 days ago): Onset of fever and generalized myalgia.  
  • Ongoing: Night sweats, daytime sweats, intermittent chills, nausea with poor oral intake, fatigue. Minimal response to paracetamol/ibuprofen.

- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia/Drooling: Denied.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Chronic seasonal rhinitis only (pollen).  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing/dyspnea: Denied.  
  • Swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face): Denied.  
  • Ear symptoms: Denies ear pain or hearing changes.  
  • Neck pain/swelling/stiffness: Denies stiffness or swelling.  
  • Other: Denies cough, cold symptoms, sore throat.

- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • No prior similar febrile illness or ENT emergencies reported.  
  • Current febrile episode managed only with OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented). No prior ED visits or adrenaline use.

- Allergies and current medications:
  • Allergies: Pollen (seasonal hay fever). No known drug allergies reported.  
  • Medications: Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented); Paracetamol (OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented); Ibuprofen (OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented).

- Social context:
  • Works as a nurse; experiencing work-limiting fatigue.  
  • Non-smoker; moderate alcohol intake; performs moderate exercise several times weekly.

Objective:
- Observable swelling/distribution: Not reported.  
- Airway/breathing: No stridor, dyspnea, or respiratory distress reported.  
- Mental status: Alert and oriented during call.  
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (telephone consult; no physical exam performed).  
- Accompaniment: None; patient spoke alone from private location.

Assessment:
- Pyrexia of unknown origin post-travel; differential includes malaria and other tropical or systemic infections.  
- No current evidence of ENT airway compromise or localized ENT infection.  
- Hay fever (pollen allergy) noted but unrelated to present febrile illness.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Arrange in-person clinical examination at central London clinic today.  
  • Blood tests to include malaria screen (thick and thin blood films), inflammatory markers, and additional infection work-up as directed by examining clinician.  
  • Advised patient not to attend work until evaluated.

- Instructions to patient:
  • Call the provided clinic number after a few minutes to secure same-day appointment.  
  • Bring printed/accessible consultation note to show reception/triage.  
  • Maintain adequate hydration; continue antipyretics as needed.  
  • Seek emergency care (local A&E or call emergency services) if she develops worsening fever, confusion, severe headache, neck stiffness, breathing difficulty, or any new swelling of throat/lips/tongue.

- Follow-up:
  • Post-evaluation management and any ENT/allergy referral dependent on examination findings.  
  • Employer sick leave and return-to-work guidance to follow after diagnosis.

Quality checks:
● Missing but clinically expected elements:
  – Vital signs (temperature, pulse, BP, respiratory rate, O₂ saturation).  
  – Physical examination including oropharyngeal, cervical lymph nodes, and tympanic membranes.  
  – Detailed medication doses and exact malaria prophylaxis taken.  
  – Availability of rescue medications (e.g., epinephrine auto-injector) not relevant but typically documented for allergic presentations.

● Internal conflicts: None noted.

● Transcript quality: Clear; minor background pauses but overall intelligible.
